record.original_question: For a centered multivariate Gaussian random vector X = (X1, ..., Xn) on R^n with positive-definite covariance matrix Σ, which collections of conditional independence statements of the form Xi is independent of Xj given X_K, where i and j are distinct indices and K is a subset of the remaining indices, can be realized? Equivalently, characterize the Gaussian conditional independence models: semi-algebraic subsets of the cone PD_n of real positive-definite symmetric n×n matrices defined by equations det(Σ_{{i}∪K,{j}∪K}) = 0, where this determinant is the almost-principal minor associated with the conditional independence statement Xi independent of Xj given X_K.

evidence.quote: An almost-principal minor of Σ is a subdeterminant which has row indices {i} ∪ K and column indices {j} ∪ K for some K ⊂ {1, . . . , n} and i, j ∈ {1, . . . , n}\K. We denote this subdeterminant by [i ⊥⊥ j |K ].
The general question behind this asks for characterization of all conditional independence models which can be realized by Gaussians on R^n.
General Problem: Study the geometry of conditional independence models for multivariate Gaussian random variables.
A Gaussian conditional independence model, or GCI model for short, is any semi-algebraic subset of the cone PDn which can be defined by polynomial equations of the form [i⊥⊥ j |K ] = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X = (X_1, \dots, X_n)$ be a centered Gaussian random vector on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with positive-definite covariance matrix $\Sigma \in \mathrm{PD}_n$, where $\mathrm{PD}_n$ denotes the cone of real symmetric positive-definite $n\times n$ matrices. For distinct indices $i,j \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ and a subset $K \subseteq \{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\{i,j\}$, the conditional independence statement "$X_i \perp\!\!\!\perp X_j \mid X_K$" holds if and only if the almost-principal minor
$$[i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K] \;:=\; \det\bigl(\Sigma_{\{i\}\cup K,\;\{j\}\cup K}\bigr) \;=\; 0,$$
where $\Sigma_{A,B}$ denotes the submatrix of $\Sigma$ with row indices $A$ and column indices $B$.

Define a Gaussian conditional independence (GCI) model to be any semi-algebraic subset of $\mathrm{PD}_n$ that can be cut out by polynomial equations of the form $[i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K] = 0$.

Problem: Characterize all collections $\mathcal{C}$ of conditional independence statements $\{i \perp\!\!\!\perp j \mid K\}$ that are realizable in the sense that there exists $\Sigma \in \mathrm{PD}_n$ for which the set of CI statements holding for $\Sigma$ equals $\mathcal{C}$. Equivalently, give a description of the GCI models as semi-algebraic subsets of $\mathrm{PD}_n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general characterization of realizable Gaussian conditional independence structures is open. It is known there is no finite complete axiomatization of Gaussian CI relations (Šimeček; Sullivant), and the CI implication problem is undecidable. Realizability of gaussoids has been characterized only for small $n$ (e.g., $n=4$); no general forbidden-minor or finite characterization is known for larger ground sets.

status_evidence.title: Gaussian conditional independence relations have no finite complete characterization
status_evidence.snippet: There can be no finite list of CI relations from which all Gaussian CI implications can be deduced.
status_evidence.claim: No finite axiomatization of Gaussian CI relations exists, indicating the characterization problem is highly nontrivial.

status_evidence.title: Classes of Gaussian, Discrete and Binary Representable Independence Models Have No Finite Characterization
status_evidence.snippet: Classes of representable independence models have no finite characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Supports that the realizability characterization is not achievable by any finite scheme.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Conditional Independence and Weak Realizations of Multivariate Gaussian Random Variables
status_evidence.snippet: Studies CI and weak realizations of multivariate Gaussians.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to study realizability, indicating the general problem remains active and open.
